It's dead. Your brother stole it again.
You went somewhere, when it was inside your head. Where?
It wanted my father. The little I had of him. And to take it, it had to look... and it showed me.
An inn. Smoke, mead, blackberries. I was small, sitting at a table far too big for me. And him, on a little stage, with a lute.
Never his face. But I heard him. He sang a lullaby... to me, in front of all those people.
Your mother told you never to listen to his melody.
She did. And an hour ago I couldn't have hummed a note of it. Now I remember every word.
